scope: Analytic cone/cone (frustum) surface-surface intersection (seventh analytic SS slice, one cell): native intersect_cone_cone in crates/brep-core/src/intersections/cone_cone.rs, bridge op brep_intersect_cone_cone, typed TS adapter intersectConeCone (transport-only). Both operands reuse the canonical conical-frustum recognizer of plane_cone::recognize_cone unchanged (four ruled rational-quadratic side patches on the linear radius taper, a bilinear cap per nonzero ring, true apex admitted, equal-radius frustum refused as a cylinder; rigid affine placements admitted). Coaxial configuration only, in either axis orientation (apex-to-apex and base-to-base anti-axial pairs are oriented by the sign of the axes' dot product and classified the same way): parallelism is certified on the cross-product magnitude and axiality on the perpendicular offset with the sphere/cylinder snap discipline (pure-rounding tilts/offsets snap, recognition-scale ones report near_coincidence, clearly non-parallel or off-axis pairs are unsupported_surface — the general cone/cone pair is a quartic, out of scope, and there is no numerical fallback). In the shared axial coordinate s each side carries the linear radius profile rho_i(s) between its rings, so side contacts solve the single linear equation rho_1(s) == rho_2(s). Different tapers give at most one height s*, reported as the exact rational circle of radius rho(s*) when s* is certified strictly inside both height ranges (a root clipped by either finite height is honestly absent); a root within the band of any of the four ring planes is a rim contact, and a root whose radius collapses into the band is the apex-meeting contact — both stay tangency_or_multiple_root, never a guessed circle. Equal tapers inside the band make the profiles parallel: coincident over the overlapping height range reports coincident_trim (never a surface component), clearly distinct profiles resolve empty, and equality at a single ring plane only is the rim tangency, unresolved; a strict sign change at near-equal taper is ill-conditioned and stays tangency_or_multiple_root. Any two ring planes (one per cone) coinciding within the band carry a rim/rim, rim-on-cap or apex-on-cap boundary contact and stay tangency_or_multiple_root independent of the side classification, and a band-thin or negative axial overlap reduces to the facing-plane touch. Resolved contacts are exact rational circles (four 90-degree arcs, weights cos(pi/4)) with iso-v lifts on all four side patches of both cones and a 16-sample residual bound against both side profile equations. Nothing here authorizes a topology change.
coverage: RESOLVED cone/cone different tapers: frustum r 1->3 over z 0..6 (rho = 1 + s/3) against frustum r 4->2 over z 1..5 (rho = 4.5 - s/2) solves the linear side equation into the single exact circle at s* = 4.2 (radius 2.4), center/radius to 1e-12 against the closed-form oracle, 16 samples on both implicit side equations to 1e-12, iso-v lifts at v = 0.7 on all four side patches of the first cone and v = 0.8 on the second, every lifted UV point verified through both placed patch surfaces to 1e-9

RESOLVED cone/cone anti-axial pair: frustum r 2->4 flipped down (axis -z, own bottom ring at z=8, rho = 2 + (8 - s)/3 over s in [2,8]) against frustum r 1->3 over z 0..6 yields the exact circle at s* = 5.5 (radius 17/6) to 1e-12 with iso-v lifts at v = 11/12 and v = 5/12 — apex-to-apex/base-to-base orientations classify identically after orienting by the axes' dot sign

RESOLVED cone/cone clipped root: frustum r 3->1 over z 0..6 against frustum r 4->2 over z 2..4 has its linear root at s* = 4.5 beyond the second cone's top ring — honestly absent, empty and numerically_resolved; a clear 0.5 axial gap between the facing ring planes also resolves empty

RESOLVED rigid placement: the crossing configuration rotated about X and translated keeps the exact circle against the independent binary64 oracle to 1e-12 with UV lifts verified through both placed surfaces to 1e-9
UNRESOLVED equal-taper coincident profiles: frustum r 5/3->11/3 over z 2..8 carries the same profile as r 1->3 over z 0..6 across the overlap z 2..6 — coincident_trim, never a surface component

UNRESOLVED rim contacts: stacked base-to-top frusta with equal ring radii 3 at the shared plane z=6 (rim/rim), unequal ring radii at the shared plane (rim circle inside the larger cap disk), and a bottom ring lying exactly on the other cone's side (r=2 at z=3 on rho = 1 + s/3 with the steeper taper 1/2) all stay tangency_or_multiple_root, never guessed circles
UNRESOLVED apex meeting: two true-apex cones apex-to-apex at the origin (anti-axial) stay tangency_or_multiple_root, never a point or circle

UNRESOLVED near-coaxial bands: a 1e-10 perpendicular offset and a 1e-10 rad tilt inside the recognition band report near_coincidence, never forced coaxial; a pure-rounding 1e-14 offset snaps and resolves the same circle as the exact pair

REFUSED non-canonical operands and non-coaxial pairs: an equal-radius frustum (a cylinder) as either operand, sphere/tube/cuboid/torus operands, a 0.5 off-axis parallel pair and a 0.5 rad tilted pair are explicit unsupported_surface regions over the concatenated UV box, never a numerical fallback; a structurally perturbed cone is a hard validation error

WASM roundtrip: bridge reports carry kind=circle with exact curves and oracle fields, firstUv/secondUv lifts, maxSampleResidual <= 1e-12; JSON roundtrip preserves the components and regions; coverage, permitsTopologyChange=false and evidence serialize identically
behaviorChange: New read-only query intersectConeCone (brep_intersect_cone_cone); no existing query, op, or adapter behavior changed. Both dist budgets hold (geometry chunk 2,439,363 to 2,439,918 bytes measured, +555 for the coaxial classification and exact circle components reusing the shared cone recognizer — budget stays 2,445,000; total 4,757,897 to 4,758,452 bytes measured — budget stays 4,765,000).

limits.classificationBand: both recognition deviations + 16 binary64 epsilons of the axial/height/radius scale
limits.coaxialSnap: 64 binary64 epsilons of the scale on the perpendicular offset (pure-rounding only) and 64 binary64 epsilons on the axis cross-product magnitude; recognition-scale tilts/offsets report near_coincidence, larger ones are unsupported_surface
limits.sideClassification: one linear equation rho_1(s) == rho_2(s) in the shared axial coordinate: different tapers admit at most one root, exact circle only when strictly inside both height ranges; roots within the band of any ring plane (rim) or with radius collapsing into the band (apex) stay tangency_or_multiple_root; equal tapers classify coincident_trim / empty / single-plane rim tangency on the outward band
limits.ringPlaneClassification: any two ring planes (one per cone) coinciding within the band carry a rim/rim, rim-on-cap or apex-on-cap boundary contact — tangency_or_multiple_root independent of the side classification; a band-thin or negative axial overlap reduces to the facing-plane touch

limitations: Canonical coaxial operands only: both cones are the exact canonical conical frustum solid (true apex admitted, equal-radius frustum refused as a cylinder) with certified parallel coincident axes under rigid affine placement; everything else — including any parallel off-axis or non-parallel cone/cone pair (a quartic) — is an explicit unsupported_surface region, never a numerical fallback

Tangency is never a point or a guessed circle: rim contacts (root on a ring plane, coincident ring planes of any radius relation), apex meetings and ill-conditioned near-equal-taper crossings all stay tangency_or_multiple_root, and the classification band widens with both recognition deviations so near-tangent configurations below ~1e-13 of the scale stay unresolved rather than guessed
Profile coincidence over the overlap reports coincident_trim and never emits a surface component; cap/cap coincidence is only detected as a ring-plane tangency region, not a trimmed surface

NumericallyResolved is not certified complete-domain coverage and permitsTopologyChange stays false; consuming these sections in Booleans and the remaining analytic SS pairs (torus family, non-coaxial cone/cone, non-parallel cylinder/cylinder) stay open
